final.answer: The hottest liquid you can put through P-1-2 is 160°F (71°C). This is the pump's 'Maximum Temperature of Liquid Pumped' rating from its datasheet (Gorman-Rupp), and it is set by the mechanical seal's materials — silicon carbide faces with fluorocarbon (Viton) elastomers, plus a stainless steel 316 shaft sleeve and spring. Note that this temperature figure carries a footnote: for applications exceeding the maximum indicated pressure and/or temperature, the factory should be consulted. Also, the pump's pressure ratings (250 psi max operating, 266 psi max casing) apply only up to 100°F (37°C); above that, consult the factory.

final.answer: The transmitter feeding FIC-12-1 is FT-12-1, a Rosemount 3051 4-20 mA HART transmitter. On a detected failure its analog output is driven either high or low, but the direction is not fixed by design — it is user-selectable. You change the alarm direction with a jumper/switch on the transmitter. The alarm levels depend on the setting: default high alarm is ≥21.75 mA and low alarm ≤3.75 mA (high default ≥22.5 mA for some option codes); with NAMUR-compliant options it is high ≥22.5 mA and low ≤3.6 mA. Note that the alarm direction is also fixed at ordering time by option code — C4 = high alarm, CN = low alarm, CT = Rosemount standard low alarm, CR/CS = custom high/low alarm.
